rule: Flip the image horizontally while working to catch features that drift or melt to one side.
To draw heads well, know how the skull looks from every angle and fit the features piece by piece into that skull shape.
Shade in three grey values (light, medium, dark); too many values break the balance of the shading.
After flat colours, pick a light source and add flat shadows using big simple shapes.
Shaded areas are parts hidden from the light source, not areas that are simply dark coloured.
Thicker lines on parts such as the bottom of the arms give the character weight and the illusion of form.
